headline: Dry all week, warming to 5–15 degrees above average with Santa Ana winds on Thanksgiving and Friday, while record-breaking King Tides and a big incoming swell bring major, locally extreme coastal flooding to the Orange and San Diego County beaches Tuesday through Friday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Monday's early showers were light, mostly over San Diego and Orange counties, topping out at 0.14 inch at North Island and Point Loma and 0.10 inch or less farther north and inland. The rest of Monday night is dry, with scattered high clouds passing over that clear out by late Tuesday morning. Tuesday warms another 3–5 degrees, and east winds gust locally to about 35 mph early Tuesday on the coast-facing foothill slopes before easing around 10 AM.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: On Wednesday a low-pressure system aloft pushes the area of high pressure east, but it isn't expected to bring any significant weather: it stays dry, with just slight cooling west of the mountains, including the coast and valleys. High pressure rebuilds Thanksgiving (Thursday), turning winds offshore and bringing mainly weak, locally moderate Santa Ana winds (dry northeast winds blowing from inland toward the coast), strongest on Thursday, with gusts of 35–45 mph in the mountains, foothills and passes and 45 mph gusts limited to the usual windy spots. Thursday and Friday are the warmest days, 5–15 degrees above average and warmest Friday, with highs from the mid to upper 70s to the mid 80s west of the mountains.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday stays dry but cools a few degrees as low pressure starts pushing the high-pressure area east. On Sunday, about 60 percent of computer model runs bring a storm system into Northern California, the scenario most likely to give Southern California light rain, while the other 40 percent keep it away; the forecast includes a chance of rain Sunday, with low confidence in the details. A generally unsettled pattern may continue through much of next week, the first week of December, with chances for more rain, cooler weather and westerly winds.

coast: Coastal flooding is the big hazard this week on the Orange County and San Diego County coasts. Morning high tides have already reached 7.73 feet at La Jolla and will climb to 7.9–8.3 feet Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday, about 1.1–1.2 feet above normal predictions, and will likely break the all-time tide records set in late October. Surf stays around 2–5 feet through Wednesday morning, then a large, long-period west swell (8–9 feet every 18–19 seconds) arrives late Wednesday into Thursday, bringing 6–8 foot breakers Thursday with sets of 10–12 feet on exposed west-facing beaches, lowering to 3–6 feet Friday. A Coastal Flood Advisory (moderate to locally major flooding at Tuesday morning's high tide) runs until 4 AM Tuesday, followed by a Coastal Flood Warning from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM Friday for major flooding, with locally extreme flooding expected during Thursday morning's high tide; a High Surf Advisory covers the San Diego County coast from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM Friday. For boaters, no hazards are expected through Tuesday; a Small Craft Advisory covers the outer waters (10–60 miles out, including San Clemente Island) from 10 AM Wednesday to 10 AM Thursday for combined seas of 8–12 feet and northwest winds of about 23–29 mph (20–25 knots) near San Clemente Island Wednesday afternoon and evening, with seas falling below 10 feet by Thursday evening.
watch_for: Major, locally extreme coastal flooding at the morning high tides Tuesday through Friday, worst Thursday when record tides meet 10–12 foot surf sets.
Santa Ana wind gusts of 35–45 mph in the mountains, foothills and passes on Thanksgiving and Friday, with warm, dry conditions.
Low-confidence chance of light rain Sunday and a possibly wetter, cooler start to December.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in dry weather through Saturday and in the record tides and coastal flooding, fairly confident in mostly weak Santa Ana winds Thursday and Friday despite some uncertainty in where the low-pressure system sits, and have low confidence in the details of rain chances Sunday into next week.
